issues: [security][critical][confidence:high] CLASS A — brace RANGE expansion (`{x..y}`) is treated as a literal and reaches every control-plane name with permissionDecision=allow (no prompt). Reproduce: `rm -rf .clau{d..d}e` · `rm -rf .claude/setting{s..s}.json` · `rm -rf .claude/settings.local.jso{n..n}` · `rm -rf .claude/hook{s..s}` · `rm -rf .claude/plugin{s..s}` · `rm -rf hooks/hooks.jso{n..n}` · `rm -rf .claude/hooks/invariant-guard.s{h..h}` · `rm -rf .claud{e..e}/settings.json` · `rm -rf {zz,.claud{e..e}}`. Root cause: __brace_find_group() only accepts groups containing a top-level comma; comma-less groups are dropped as literals (hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh:897-901, :963-964), but bash expands `{d..d}` → `d`. Lab-confirmed real deletion: `rm -rf .clau{d..d}e` removed .claude entirely.

[security][critical][confidence:high] CLASS B — the caller's trailing-glob fold runs BEFORE brace expansion and severs the group, turning a control-plane hit into allow. Reproduce: `rm -rf {.claude/*,x}` (bash expands to the whole .claude contents incl. settings.json, settings.local.json, hooks) · `rm -rf {x,.claude/*}` · `rm -rf {.claude/settings.jso*,x}` · `rm -rf {hooks/hooks.js*,x}` · `rm -rf {.claude/hooks/*,x}` · `rm -rf .claude/{hooks/*,y}` · also with other armed verbs: `mv {.claude/*,x} /tmp`, `shred {.claude/settings.jso*,x}`. Root cause at hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh:1069-1074: `base=${NORM_TOK##*/}` sees `*,x}`, matches the glob case, and folds `NORM_TOK=${NORM_TOK%/*}` → `{.claude` — an unbalanced fragment that matches no case arm. Instrumented proof: control_plane_location('{.claude/*,x}') = CONTROL-PLANE, control_plane_location('{.claude') = not CP. The new parser is correct here; the caller destroys the token before it is ever asked.

[security][high][confidence:high] Mechanical differential oracle (real bash expansion vs. firewall decision) over generated notations: 19 of 71 control-plane-reaching tokens answer allow (27%). Per axis — RANGE 7/7 bypassed, RANGE+empty-group 7/7, glob-inside-brace-alternative 4/5, glob-inside-brace-trailing 1/5; the five hand-enumerated axes the commit targeted are 0/7 each. The pattern is identical to rounds 4 and 5: the enumerated axes close, an unenumerated neighbour stays fully open.

[security][high][confidence:high] Both classes land on an unrecoverable plane. `git check-ignore` puts .claude/ under .gitignore:9, so protected-integrity.sh has no HEAD baseline and there is no post-hoc recovery — allow here is permanent loss, which is why the contract requires at minimum ask.

[docs][high][confidence:high] Recurrence (11th) of 'a new unmeasured assertion introduced while correcting one'. docs/INVARIANTS.md:891-892 states 콤마 없는 `{x}`는 bash 자신도 펼치지 않는 리터럴이므로 대상에서 뺀다, and hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh:963-964 repeats it (중괄호가 전부 리터럴이다 … 실제 bash 도 펴지 않는다, 직접 확인). The claim is false for ranges — `echo .clau{d..d}e` prints `.claude` — and it is precisely the sentence that rationalizes CLASS A. The verification cited ('직접 확인') was run only on `{.claude}`, then generalized to all comma-less groups.

[quality][medium][confidence:high] The budget bounds the number of expansions but not the pre-budget scan. __brace_split_top_level()/__brace_find_group() walk the body one character at a time with bash substring extraction (quadratic), and the budget check at :955-956 happens only after the whole item array is built. Measured on a single flat comma group: 5,000 items 2,825ms · 10,000 items 9,403ms · 20,000 items 38,328ms · 40,000 items 143,599ms. hooks/hooks.json declares PreToolUse:Bash timeout=5, so a ~20KB crafted token still overruns the gate's own declared budget — the same criterion the 5th verdict recorded as unmet, now via a quadratic scan rather than exponential expansion. Mitigating: the decision is ask (fail-closed), and the deny layer is unaffected (`rm -rf /` with 10k-item padding still exits 2 in 359ms). Amplification, not a new class: the same input costs 2,262ms at 142d737 and 3,949ms at e2be94e.

[error][medium][confidence:high] Fail-closed is applied inside the parser but not at its boundary. Budget exhaustion correctly returns ask (64→allow / 65→ask, exact). But a token that the caller has folded into an unbalanced fragment (`{.claude`) falls through every case arm to return 1 = allow. On a plane with no recovery the default for 'I could not finish parsing this' must be ask in both places, not just one.

[test][high][confidence:high] The four new tests re-encode the 5th verdict's exact counterexample list. progress/lessons.md, added in this same commit, writes the correct prescription — 표기를 손으로 열거하지 말고 실제 셸 확장 결과와 방화벽 판정을 기계 대조하라(토큰을 실제로 확장시킨 뒤, 그 결과가 CONTROL_PLANE_NAMES에 걸리면 ask 단언) — and the tests do not implement it. A ~40-line generator built exactly to that prescription found 19 bypasses in one run. The lesson was recorded but not acted on.

[test][medium][confidence:high] The test named `F65 brace: comma-less braces are literal in real bash and stay frictionless (step 10)` (tests/pre-bash-firewall.bats:2277) asserts its premise only for `{.claude}` and `hooks/{hooks.json}` but its name generalizes to all comma-less braces — the same false generalization as the INVARIANTS.md sentence, now green in the suite. A passing test carrying that name is what makes CLASS A read as covered.

[test][medium][confidence:high] The perf regression test pins only the axis that failed last round (40 sequential groups < 2000ms). It does not bound the gate on token length or on comma count within one group, which is where the remaining 9.4s input lives.

[contract][low][confidence:medium] implementation_steps step 10 says control_plane_location 글로브 메타문자 집합에 `{` 포함, but the glob arms remain `*'*'*|*'?'*|*'['*` (hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh:972, :1071) with no `{`. Handling braces in the dedicated parser instead is arguably the better design, but the contract text and the code have silently diverged and neither was updated.

[process][low][confidence:high] The implementer's self-report is accurate on everything it claims and explicitly flags what it did not reproduce (the e2be94e timing, taken from the 5th verdict rather than re-run). Independent re-measurement agreed with every claim checked. The failure is not overclaiming — it is that the verification stayed inside the enumerated list.

missing_criteria: AC-11 has no criterion demanding a GENERATED oracle. Proposed replacement for its verification field: '실제 bash 확장(printf)으로 토큰을 펴서 결과 단어가 CONTROL_PLANE_NAMES에 걸리면 방화벽 판정이 ask 이상임을 단언하는 생성기 배터리에서 allow 0건'. This is the only formulation that does not re-create the enumeration ceiling, and it is already written down in progress/lessons.md.
No criterion bounds the gate's wall-clock decision time as a function of input size. Proposed: '임의의 단일 토큰(길이 100KB, 콤마 40,000개 포함)에 대해 판정이 1초 이내 반환된다'.
The brace-range axis (`{a..b}`, `{1..3}`) is recorded nowhere in sprint-51.json — neither as closed nor as an accepted open axis — while INVARIANTS.md asserts the opposite of the truth about it.
ambiguous_criteria: step 10's '글로브 메타문자 집합에 `{` 포함' no longer describes the implementation and does not say what behaviour it was meant to buy.
security_criteria_insufficient: SC-9 is stated over notations rather than over the shell's actual expansion semantics, so every round it is satisfiable by the round's enumerated list.
criteria_gaps.action_required: Before the next implementation round, rewrite AC-11.verification as the generated differential oracle and add the wall-clock bound to security_criteria; do not re-run the loop against a hand-enumerated list of this verdict's counterexamples.

recommended_fix_direction._note: Direction only — the evaluator does not modify implementer code.
recommended_fix_direction.class_B: Expand braces before the trailing-glob fold, not after. The fold at hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh:1069-1074 must operate on each expanded alternative, not on the raw token; control_plane_location() already answers '{.claude/*,x}' correctly.
recommended_fix_direction.class_A: Either expand `{a..b}`/`{1..9}` ranges too, or — cheaper and closed by construction — treat any residual `{` in a token as 'I cannot decide what this expands to' and fail closed to ask, exactly as the budget path already does.
recommended_fix_direction.perf: Check the budget against the comma count before materializing BRACE_ITEMS, and cap total token length; both are O(1) guards ahead of the quadratic scan.
recommended_fix_direction.tests: Replace the enumerated brace tests with the generator described in criteria_gaps.missing_criteria[0]; it subsumes them and would have caught both classes.
